review.reviewer: Codex implementation owner, design self-review informed by independent T3/T5 design
review.decision: Bind the automatic rotation briefing to the persisted request and its exact original successor, and submit it at most once through the guarded native wake path.
review.notes: Keep rotation success timing as it is. Restrict this change to the rotation briefing. Test with a private HOME and receivers that never contact a real agent or terminal. The independent design and this pre-implementation review do not establish the cause of any live missed handoff.

cases.description: A queued rotation briefing preserves the original request, recipient and deadline at the native boundary
cases.setup: Persist a synthetic sent rotation, queue a briefing under the shared lease, and replace the recipient before later drain. Use fixed time, a fake pane and a fake receiver with an observable final guard. Compare the matching recipient, exact deadline, missing or replaced request, changed agent, Home, SID, or pane instance. Include a change inside native preparation and unusable composer or native route.
cases.action: Drain with the existing automatic wake entry after releasing the lease. Inspect exact receiver options and count native input, paste, Enter and final queue states.
cases.expected: The exact still-current successor before the original deadline can receive one idle wake. Mismatches or unavailable evidence cannot mutate input. The existing user draft and active/idle gate remain authoritative. A definite refusal is retained separately from possible submission; neither case retries or falls back to keys.

cases.description: The bound briefing cannot replay an unknown submission or contaminate ordinary notifications
cases.setup: Return a positive refusal or unknown result from the fake native receiver; queue an ordinary workspace reminder and a protected Relay notice. Repeatedly observe, recover, and drain the private queue.
cases.action: Count receiver calls and check stored claim, receipt and batch contents across the original attempt and subsequent drains.
cases.expected: The original unknown claim remains protected under its own batch identity. A definite refusal does not become unknown or authorize automatic retry. Independent ordinary notifications and protected Relay retain their own normal submission opportunity.
